findings.evidence: You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the covered purchase amount after that monthly review.
findings.fix: Pick one term for the item being reimbursed and use it in all three sentences.
findings.violation: Three different terms (stipend item, reimbursable item, covered purchase amount) name what is apparently the same single artifact across three consecutive sentences, with no defined-terms signal that they mean the same thing.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout.
findings.fix: Rewrite the opening sentence to state the topic the rest of the paragraph covers.
findings.violation: The paragraph's opening sentence shares almost no vocabulary with the rest of the paragraph, so it does not preview the paragraph's actual topic.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter.
findings.fix: Remove the three sentences unrelated to stipend coordination, or move them to sections about their own topics.
findings.violation: The section's four sentences pursue four unrelated themes (stipend coordination, a past travel audit, federal remote-work guidance, and the office coffee budget) with nothing connecting them, so a reader finishing the section cannot state what it was actually about.

findings.evidence: Also, you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days. You track its status there until the payment clears.
findings.fix: Name the actor explicitly, for example The manager countersigns the request within two business days, so the employee reader can tell the instruction is not theirs to act on.
findings.violation: The paragraph otherwise addresses the employee directly as you, but the imperative Countersign the employee request has no stated actor and reads as an instruction to a different reader, such as the manager, interleaved without separation from the employee's own instructions.
